text:
alex: Quick q — we just hit a customer bug where a console rollout and a feature-flag both matched, and behavior was inconsistent. Who owns the final routing decision?

marta: short answer: nobody single-handedly owns it today. We have layered configs: route-level rollout policy, tenant feature-flags, and then runtime header overrides. We haven't codified precedence.

sam: Ugh. That explains the surprise. The SDK will set X-Redwood-Variant sometimes, and the console rollout also manipulates traffic. We need deterministic evaluation order.

julia: Proposal: runtime-request overrides (explicit headers) should win at eval time, then console rollouts, then tenant flags, then defaults. Guards (safety checks) should always be evaluated last to reject unsafe combos.

kevin: I worry about ownership. If console policies override tenant flags, product teams will be blocked when infra ops tries to canary. Can we add a "source" + "priority" on policies so we can reason about who can preempt whom?

alex: +1 on explicit source metadata. Also we need the console to show the "effective policy" for any request (like git's merged view). Right now it's opaque.

marta: Agreed. Minimal API change: include a small envelope on rollout configs, e.g.:

```
{
  "id": "r-123",
  "policy": [{"type":"percent","target":5}],
  "metadata": {"source":"console","owner":"release-team","priority":100}
}
```

This lets runtime show the applied source and let us sort by priority.

sam: Also add applied_by/applied_at to eval logs so we can trace which layer made the decision. A tiny sample log line: `eval: r-123 applied_by=console priority=100 request_id=...`

julia: UX note — console should surface conflicts inline: "tenant-flag X wants 50% but console forces 10% (higher priority)" and show a quick "why" (owner, change diff, audit link).

kevin: We should update policy enforcement: if guard rejects, it should provide a deterministic fallback: either block or route to fallback model. That fallback policy should also carry source info.

alex: Can we also define defaults for priority ranges? e.g., system/core policies 1000, console rollouts 500, tenant flags 200, SDK/runtime overrides 900? We should avoid overlap.

marta: Yep. I'll draft a precedence table. But we should avoid magic numbers in UI — show human labels (system, runtime-override, console, tenant).

ops-bot: deploy-notice: rollout r-123 promoted to canary in us-west at 2026-11-02T14:30Z

sam: One more ask: add `effective_config` endpoint that returns the merged policy for a given request context (user, route, headers). That will make debugging much easier.

kevin: If we add `source` metadata we must also add RBAC checks: only owners of console policies can set priority above a threshold. Don't let product teams escalate over infra without review.

alex: Actionables: Marta to draft precedence table + API envelope; Sam to spec logging changes (applied_by/applied_at/effective_reason); Julia to mock console UX for conflict visualization; Kevin to propose RBAC thresholds. We'll sync tomorrow.

marta: noted — I'll put a short doc in the eng-platform folder and ping here when ready. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks all — this should cut down the surprise behavior in the wild.
